notes.stream_power.erodibility: K in m/Myr per (km3/yr)^area_exponent, per unit slope (the kernel divides the discharge in m3/yr by 1e9). Derivation: the tectonic engine's river law is river_erosion = 15 m/Myr per km of sqrt(catchment km2) with uniform runoff; with discharge Q = r P A in km3/yr and a reference runoff depth r P = 0.4 m/yr = 4e-4 km/yr (the coefficient law's value at P = 1 m/yr; with runoff.budyko the world's runoff differs from cell to cell, so the match to the engine holds where the runoff is near 0.4 m/yr), Q = 4e-4 x A(km2), so the same incision needs K = 15 / sqrt(4e-4) = 750. Correction of erosion plan step D0 (2026-10-07): from Phase A to Phase C the default was 24 = 15 / sqrt(0.4), which took P as 1 instead of 1e-3 km/yr and made the fluvial term 31.6 times too weak. Calibration record before the correction (step A6, 2026-10-06, 256 columns, 20 Myr): erosion run 1 at K = 24 gave a land-mean denudation of 4.03 m/Myr and run 2 at K = 100 gave 4.26 m/Myr, with the hillslope diffusion carrying most of it at 20 km cells.
notes.stream_power.crust_class_multiplier_*: K is multiplied by the multiplier of the cell's geosphere.crust_class (continental, transitional, oceanic).
notes.stream_power.crust_age_factor: K is multiplied by 1 + crust_age_factor x crust_age / 1000 Myr; 0 turns the age factor off.
notes.stream_power.slope_exponent: n; Phase A implements n = 1 only (the implicit step is linear in the slope) and the kernel rejects other values.
notes.hillslope.critical_slope: 0 turns the limiter off; otherwise the diffusion acts on max(0, gradient - critical_slope).
notes.runoff: With budyko false: runoff = coefficient x annual precipitation x (1 - snow_reduction x snow fraction) x (1 - ice_reduction x ice fraction); the snow fraction is the share of the seasons with a mean temperature below snow_temperature_c, the ice fraction is 1 where every season is below it. With budyko true (the default since erosion plan C2) the runoff is Fu's curve (runoff.budyko) and coefficient, snow_reduction and ice_reduction are not read by the routing; coefficient stays the unit of the legacy flow conversion in hydrology.rivers (a mean-sized cell under 1 mm/month contributes 1 / river_factor units at coefficient 0.4, the Phase A law). snow_temperature_c also sets the seasonal snow rule of hydrology.rivers. The potential evaporation (PET) of the runoff, the transmission losses and the lake balance is one law, the open-water law of lakes.evaporation_* applied to each season's temperature and averaged over the year. The rainfall solver's bulk-aerodynamic potential evaporation (atmosphere.potential_evaporation) is 2 to 5 times Earth's over dry land (land medians of 6 to 7 m/yr at 20 to 40 C on the 256-column Earth run, which left the Mississippi about 6 mm/yr of runoff) and is not used: it stays a climate diagnostic.
notes.erosion.uplift_m_myr: Uniform rock uplift during the erosion run, added to the engine's rate (engine_uplift_scale x geosphere.rock_uplift_rate); 0 since Phase A.
notes.erosion.engine_uplift_scale: Erosion plan D1: U per cell = uplift_m_myr + engine_uplift_scale x geosphere.rock_uplift_rate (m/Myr, signed: the tectonic engine's 10 Myr mean elevation change before its surface processes; negative is subsidence). 1 takes the engine's rate as it is; 0 restores the former uplift 0 (with uplift_m_myr 0).
notes.isostasy.*: Erosion plan C8: local Airy compensation of the erosion run, column by column, without flexure. After each step every cell's elevation changes by rebound_fraction x the rock the step removed - loading_fraction x the sediment it laid, on land and sea (a marine deposit loads the sea floor). rebound_fraction = rho_c / rho_m = 2800 / 3300 = 0.848 from the engine's densities (tectonics::columns: continental crust 2800, mantle 3300 kg/m3). loading_fraction is the same 0.848, not the engine's sediment density (2700 / 3300 = 0.818): the kernel's volumes are rock volumes (porosity 0), so the sediment laid is the rock removed, and unequal fractions would create or destroy column (with 0.818 the land of the minimal eroded-world rose by 0.66 m on average where it should sink, because most of its erosion is laid again on land). One fraction for every crust class: the kernel erodes land only, where the crust is almost all continental or transitional, and oceanic crust's 2900 / 3300 = 0.879 differs by 4 percent. The water density is left out: under the sea a deposit replaces water and the subsidence fills with water, which for rock gives (2800 - 1030) / (3300 - 1030) = 0.780, so a marine deposit sinks about 9 percent too far (0.848 / 0.780). Local compensation is an approximation: with the engine's flexural length of 120 km a load is half compensated only at wavelengths near 530 km (fully at much longer ones, hardly at shorter ones), so local Airy over-responds to cell-scale patterns at 256 columns and finer (single peaks and narrow basins rebound or sink as if each were broad). 0 turns either part off. denudation and aggradation keep counting the rock removed and the sediment laid (the exhumation reads them); the net elevation change of the run includes the response, so the surface lowers by about (1 - rebound_fraction) of the net rock removal.
notes.rivers.minimum_flow: A cell is a river where its annual mean flow in legacy units (river_factor) reaches this; 3 is the flow of one mean-sized cell under the legacy source threshold of 40 mm/month (40 / 15 = 2.7).
notes.lakes.evaporation_*: Open-water evaporation E = evaporation_per_c x max(0, T - evaporation_zero_c) in m/yr, applied to each season's mean air temperature and averaged over the four seasons (erosion plan C2: before, to the annual mean temperature): 2.0 m/yr at 25 C, 0.9 at 10 C, 0.15 at 0 C. It is the one potential evaporation of the routing's runoff (Fu's curve), the transmission losses and the lake balance (runoff note).
notes.potentials.*_reference_rate_m_myr: The rate that maps to a score of 100: score = 100 x log10(1 + rate) / log10(1 + reference), clamped to 0..100.
notes.runoff.budyko: Erosion plan C2: true takes a cell's annual runoff depth from Fu's Budyko curve, runoff = P - AET with AET / P = 1 + PET / P - (1 + (PET / P)^w)^(1 / w) (Fu 1981; Zhang et al. 2004, Water Resources Research 40, W02502), P the annual precipitation and PET the open-water evaporation of lakes.evaporation_* applied per season and averaged over the year (runoff note). The curve gives a runoff ratio near 1 where PET is small and near 0 where PET is many times P, so it replaces the coefficient and the snow and ice reductions. budyko_w = 2.6 is the typical value Zhang et al. 2004 fit over catchments worldwide (Fu's w; larger w evaporates more). false keeps the coefficient law (runoff note).
notes.transmission.*: Erosion plan C2: losses of a river's flow to evaporation from its channel and floodplain where it crosses land drier than open water (the Sudd's role for the Nile). Each land cell loses min(flow, width x link length x deficit) before passing its flow on, with deficit = max(0, PET - P) of the cell (m/yr; PET the open-water law of the runoff note), the link length the distance to its receiver, and width = width_coefficient x (discharge in m3/s)^width_exponent, multiplied by floodplain_factor where the link's slope is below floodplain_slope; a cell of open water (hydrosphere.imported_lake) loses deficit x its area instead; a cell flooded by a depression of the routing loses nothing, because the lake balance (hydrology.lake_levels) owns its evaporation. width_coefficient 5 m per (m3/s)^0.5 and width_exponent 0.5 are the downstream hydraulic geometry of Leopold and Maddock 1953 (width = a Q^b with b about 0.5; a = 5 is a mid value of the fitted coefficients, not a fit of this world: 50 m at 100 m3/s, 500 m at 10000 m3/s). floodplain_factor 10 below floodplain_slope 2e-4 (20 cm per km, a lowland river): a lowland river's floodplain and wetlands evaporate over about ten channel widths. enabled false turns the losses off (discharge then grows monotonically downstream).
notes.rivers.baseflow_fraction: Erosion plan C2: b, the share of each cell's annual runoff released evenly through the four seasons (groundwater and the slow melt of held snow): a season's runoff = (1 - b) x the snow-rule runoff + b x annual runoff / 4, so cold-season rivers keep flowing (the 512-column run 4 had no January flow over most land north of 30N). 0.25 is a round value chosen by the Phase C session, not fitted: observed baseflow indices (the slow share of a river's flow; global analysis of Beck et al. 2013, Water Resources Research 49) are mostly higher, so it is a low estimate of the evenly released share. 0 keeps the Phase B rule.
notes.roughness.*: Erosion plan C3: relief roughness added once to the land's base elevation at the start of the erosion pass and kept in the eroded terrain (amplitude_m 0 turns it off). 3D gradient noise (Perlin 2002) sampled at each cell centre's position on the sphere, so it has no seam and no pole stretch; octave k has lattice spacing wavelength_km / 2^k and weight persistence^k, and an octave with a wavelength below twice the north-south cell size gets weight 0 (the grid does not resolve it), so the value does not depend on the grid width up to the octaves it resolves and a coarse grid carries less relief; the sum is scaled so that amplitude_m is 3.5 standard deviations of the full octave set (standard deviation amplitude_m / 3.5, about 8.6 m at 30, with every octave resolved), zero mean in expectation. A lowering is scaled by min(1, (elevation - sea level - 1 m) / amplitude_m), and a land cell is never lowered to sea level + 1 m or below; the result is held to geosphere.max_elevation. Seeded from the world seed (salt 0x5266), never from the shared random stream. 2000 km and 6 octaves at 0.6: the finest octave is about 60 km; 256 columns (156 km cells) resolve the three octaves of 500 km and more, 2048 columns all six.
notes.routing.*: Erosion plan C3. randomised: a land cell that drains to a lower neighbour takes the D-infinity gradient g (Tarboton 1997; the steepest of the eight facets formed by a cardinal and the adjacent diagonal neighbour, with the metric's distances) and draws its receiver between the facet's two neighbours, at offsets p1 and p2 in metres, the second with probability |p1 x g| / (|p1 x g| + |p2 x g|), so the mean displacement is parallel to the gradient (the intent of Rho8, Fairfield and Leymarie 1991, without its square-cell factor); the draw is a hash of the world seed (salt 0x7207) and the cell; a drawn neighbour that is neither lower nor sea gives way to the other, then to D8. resolve_flats: the cells that follow their flood receiver drain by the combined gradient of Barnes, Lehman and Mulla 2014 (twice the distance towards the flat's low edges plus the inverted distance from higher terrain), steepest descent on it over the metric's distance, lowest direction code on a tie. Raised cells (a flooded depression) form one flat per outlet, the first unraised cell on their flood chain (a depression: its spill), its only low edge; cells at their own terrain form connected flats at one filled elevation whose low edges are the adjacent cells at that elevation that drain downhill (a flat without one keeps the flood order). false keeps deterministic D8 and the flood order.
notes.routing.ocean_minimum_area_fraction: Erosion plan H3: the sea of the routing, the erosion and the lake balance is every 8-connected region (longitude wrapping, no pole crossing) of cells at or below the sea level whose area is at least this fraction of the planet's, and always the largest such region; a smaller enclosed below-sea region is a depression for the lake balance (a lake, a salt lake or a salt pan). Earth (510 million km2): the Mediterranean, 2.5 million km2, is 0.49 percent and stays sea; the Caspian, 0.37 million km2, is 0.07 percent and becomes a lake; the Black Sea, 0.44 million km2 (0.09 percent), would become a lake if the grid cut it off from the Mediterranean. 0 makes every below-sea region sea; above 1 only the largest.
notes.glacial.*: Erosion plan Phase G (section 6, 'Decided for Phase G'): glacial erosion in stream-power form after Hergarten 2021 (Earth Surface Dynamics 9, 937). enabled false passes no glacial input to the kernel (the fluvial step exactly). The ELA per cell is z + (T_warm - cooling_c - T_ela(P)) / atmosphere.lapse_rate, T_warm the warmest season's temperature at the cell's elevation z in the coarse climate, P the annual precipitation, T_ela the summer temperature at the ELA of Ohmura, Kasser and Funk 1992 (Journal of Glaciology 38, 397): P = 645 + 296 T + 9 T^2 with P in mm w.e. and T the summer free-air temperature in C (70 glaciers, standard error 200 mm), solved for T on its increasing branch. cooling_c: the mean cooling of the erosion run's climate below the coarse climate, standing for the glacial cycles of the recent geological past; 4 C is the order of the Quaternary's time-mean cooling (about 6 C at the last glacial maximum), a calibration for the user's verdict, not a fit. Ice source per land cell: runoff x area x min((H - ELA) / full_ice_range_m, 1), negative below the ELA (Hergarten's Eq. 23; 500 m is the gap of his examples, 2000 to 2500 m), accumulated downstream as max(0, source + inflow), so the terminus is where ablation has eaten the flux; ice reaching the sea calves. Thickness h = min(maximum_thickness_m, thickness_ratio x width_reference_m x (A_i / 1 km2)^width_exponent), A_i the ice flux divided by 1 m/yr: width_exponent 0.3 is Hergarten's alpha, thickness_ratio 0.25 the value of Liebl et al. 2023 (Geoscientific Model Development 16, 1315) for real glaciers, width_reference_m 400 makes a 100 km2 glacier 1.6 km wide (the Aletsch's order; round, not fitted), maximum_thickness_m 3000 caps ice sheets, which Hergarten's valley-glacier scaling does not cover. Erosion: K_eff = gamma^m x erodibility_ratio x K + (1 - gamma)^m x K with gamma = ice flux / discharge (Hergarten's Eq. 27; his examples use ratios 1 and 2), solved on the ice surface; the bed is the solved surface less h, held at or above the sea level less flotation_ratio x h (917 / 1028 kg/m3: grounded ice erodes no deeper than where it floats).
notes.marine.delta_top_m: Erosion plan C5b (progradation, fill and spill): no sea cell is raised above the sea level plus delta_top_m. On its way down the seabed a load leaves each sea cell its e-folding share (sediment_travel_km), but no more than the room left below that top (less what other outlets laid there in the same step); the rest passes on. At the walk's end (a seabed pit, the last sea cell before land, or the cell-count cap) the cell keeps what fits and the remainder spills over the sea, lowest current surface first (a priority walk over 8-connected sea cells, through full ones), filling each cell it reaches up to the top; only a remainder that reaches no sea cell below the top stays on the end cell (counted as stranded by the kernel). A cell raised so becomes land at the next routing (the sea mask is the elevation in whole metres at or below the sea level) and is marked in geosphere.prograded. 1.5 m: a delta plain stands a metre or two above the sea at its coast; 1.5 rounds to 2 m above the sea, half a metre clear of the whole-metre rule, so the routing's mask and basebelowsea agree that the cell is land.
notes.regional.halo_cells: Global cells computed around a regional window and discarded (erosion plan Phase E, section 6, 'Seams of the solve'): at least the reach of the upsampling (2 per block-mean pass: 4 with two passes; the interpolation reads the global field directly) plus the solve's catchments between pinned channels (about 2). Raised, not tuned by look, if Landscape.RegionalOverlap fails. E4: 16 with mean_passes 6 (the rule 2 x passes + 2 = 14, plus the solve's catchments).
notes.regional.noise_amplitude_m: Regional noise: octaves from twice the global north-south spacing down to twice the fine one (the global terrain already carries the longer ones); amplitude = noise_amplitude_m + noise_relief_fraction x the interpolated local global relief, tapered to zero within coast_band_m of the sea level. Initial values of Phase E, judged by the user at E4.
notes.regional.pin_area_km2: Global links whose upstream cell drains at least this area are pinned fine channels; 0 pins every land cell's link, which bounds every unpinned fine catchment to about one global cell (seams).
notes.regional.elapsed_myr: Elapsed time of the transient analytical relief (n = 1): knickpoints from the pinned channels travel upstream at K Q^m for this long; K and m are stream_power's. Without the incision (uplift_scale and denudation_rate_scale 0, Phase E to R, 1 Myr) a long time only lowers the land between the rivers towards their beds (window A of erosion run 9: mean lowering 1.6 m at 1 Myr, 30 m at 20 Myr). With R9's incision the time sets the valley depth (rate x time, capped at the local global relief) and the wave's reach (K Q^m x time, 0.15 to 1.1 km per Myr for the fine sub-catchments of a 10 km cell). It must stay below the fine response times (36 to 81 Myr for a first-order cell on erosion run 9's windows A and B): the frame of the global mean (the incision instead of a lift of the land) holds while the plateau lies beyond the wave's reach, and beyond it the relief would saturate while the frame lowers the block without bound (the relief cap bounds it). R9 (erosion run 9, windows A and B at k 16): 20 Myr, the erosion run's own length, at most; 100 Myr with the uplift alone lowered B's land by 317 m on average in the solve, 169 of its 281 global land cells reached the relief cap and the downstream consistency raised 31 cells by up to 727 m above their own rate x time (20 Myr: 7 and 1 cells reach the cap, 0 and 4 cells raised, up to 41 m). The cost does not depend on it (closed form: 17 to 19 s per window at 1, 20 and 100 Myr).
notes.regional.damping: Weight of the newest solution in the routing surface of the analytical relief's fixed point (an exponential moving average, Tzathas et al. 2024 section 5.1, which gives no value); 1 is no damping. Every pass solves from the start surface; only the surface the next routing reads is damped (erosion plan E2c).
notes.regional.mean_passes: Block-mean correction passes (erosion plan E4, measured on erosion run 9's bundle, global cells 164-183 x 48-63 at k = 16, 8.4 km of relief): the largest block-mean error of the kept window was 178 m with 2 passes, 81 m with 3, 38 m with 4 and 9.4 m with 6 (about 0.45 per pass), at 4.3 to 6.6 s per window; 6 is the first value under 10 m. Each pass widens the reach by two global cells: halo_cells must be at least 2 x mean_passes + 2 (the pass throws otherwise).
notes.regional.warp_*: Erosion plan Phase R, R2: a domain warp of the sampling positions of the global fields (a smooth vector noise on the sphere, a pure function of the fine cell's absolute position and the seed), so that the global grid's rows, columns and diagonals do not print through coasts, lake shores and ice edges. warp_amplitude_cells is the largest displacement in global cells (0: no warp, the Phase E surface), warp_wavelength_cells the warp noise's first wavelength in global cells, warp_fade_m the height from the sea level over which the elevation's warp fades to zero (0: no fade), so inland valleys stay under the pinned channels. Criterion: the block-mean error must stay under about 10 m. R2: 0.5 cells, wavelength 2, fade 300 m. Measured on erosion run 9's window A (k = 16) in the first R2 form: the warp alone barely changes the coast (box-counting dimension 0.945 against 0.940); 0.3 and 0.8 cells, wavelength 4 and fades 0 and 1000 m changed the dimension by under 0.01 and the block-mean error by under 1 m. With the R2 defaults the share of land-sea pairs on global block edges is 0.055 on A (1/k = 0.0625; R1 0.055) and no straight shore run reaches k cells (R1: 3).
notes.regional.coast_*: Erosion plan Phase R, R2 (the legacy coast lessons of plan section 6). The coast noise (persistence coast_noise_persistence, octaves from one global cell down to two fine cells) has the amplitude coast_noise_amplitude_m + coast_noise_relief_fraction x the local global relief (the legacy roughness), on the global cells whose 3 x 3 neighbourhood holds land and sea. With coast_land_share > 0 it acts only on the decision surface that sets the coastline; the elevation keeps Phase E's noise. coast_sea_drop_m pushes the decision's sea side down (so the noise does not speckle deep water) and lifts it towards global cells that may hold no fine sea (so sea does not stop along their block edges). coast_shore_floor_m: a fine cell the mask moves across the sea level is at least this deep or high (as far as the decision is), capped at its own global cell's distance from the sea level so every block can reach its mean; the other cells take the floor only in a band along the shoreline, and the sign-keeping passes never bring a cell nearer the sea level than that, so no zero-depth sheet forms. coast_land_share replaces the centre rule: a global land cell's block is at least this share land and a global sea cell's at most 1 minus it. 0 for the amplitude, the drop and the share keeps the Phase E coast (the coast_band_m taper and the centre rule). R2 values, measured in R1's order (sea before the channels) on erosion run 9 against R1's bundles (out/scratch/erosion-r/r1/A2, B2, C2): amplitude 50 m, persistence 0.6, relief fraction 0.25, drop 300 m, shore floor 20 m, share 0.5. Box-counting dimension below one global cell 1.021 on A (164-183 x 48-63, k = 16; R1 0.901 by the same probe), 1.032 on B (R1 0.886), 0.833 on C (k = 4, sizes 1 and 2 only; R1 0.763); one-cell islets 19 / 8 / 3 (R1 11 / 6 / 7); no block outside the share (R1 17 / 12 / 18), no one-cell hole away from channels (R1 13 / 3 / 14), diagonal pinches 1 / 1 / 1 (R1 4 / 3 / 20). Coastal land away from the shore (q99 of cell minus its 8 neighbours' mean): A 144 m (R1 118, inland 141), B 194 m (R1 186, inland 163), C 387 m (R1 408, inland 309); shore land cells, the step down to the sea, A 622 m (R1 143). Sea cells shallower than 1 m 62 / 18 / 33 (R1 186 / 75 / 65), than 20 m 2624 / 1284 / 413 (R1 2415 / 1229 / 386). Start-surface block-mean error 2.7 / 2.6 / 4.6 m (R1 9.4 / 7.5 / 13.2), 16.9 / 18.6 / 1.8 s per window (R1 6.5 to 7.6 s at k = 16). Relief fraction at 50 m / 0.6 (dimension and one-cell islets on A, then C): 0: 0.964, 13; 0.783, 1. 0.1: 0.975, 11; 0.835, 3. 0.25 (chosen): 1.021, 19; 0.833, 3. 0.5: 1.053, 18; 0.839, 4, and a block-mean error of 30 m on A and 32 m on C. The jagged alternative 150 m / 0.7: dimension 1.105 on A with 27 islets (islets scattered over the shelf in a side-by-side look). Earlier forms: an uncapped 20 m floor gave C 29 m; a floor interpolated between global cells left 569 zero-depth sea cells on A. Block-mean errors of the relief-fraction sweep at 50 m / 0.6 (windows A / C): 0 -> 0.30 / 0.72 m, 0.1 -> 0.19 / 4.2 m, 0.25 -> 2.7 / 4.6 m (chosen), 0.5 -> 30 / 32 m. The shore floor is a step function of the global cell, so where its cap binds (|g| under 20 m) low cells differ more across block edges than inside blocks (R2 review: sea -40..0 m 5.4 against 2.9 m on A; land 0..40 m 2.5 against 1.8 m): left for the user's look at a low coast (fix: the cap from |g| interpolated between global cells).
notes.regional.share_passes: Erosion plan Phase R, R2: the cap of the land-share offset's Jacobi passes; the passes stop when no block of the widened box misses its share (the regional bundle's diagnostics record sharepasses, the passes after which the domain met the rule, and sharemisses). The box is widened by r x share_passes + 2 + 2 x signed_passes global cells (r = 1 for k >= 3, 2 for k <= 2), so the result does not depend on the window. Erosion run 9: 6, 6 and 4 passes on windows A, B and C; 1 to 4 on the synthetic test windows.
notes.regional.signed_passes: Erosion plan Phase R, R2: the sign-keeping block-mean passes after the land-share mask (each moves a cell at most 90 per cent of the way to the sea level, a method constant); they restore the block means the mask's clamp and the shore move. Window A: 22 m block-mean error with 6 passes, 2.6 m with 12.
notes.regional.meander_*: Erosion plan Phase R, R3 (the legacy scheme: a link is drawn as two legs, each inside its own global cell's block, from the cell's junction to the edge point it shares with the receiver and on to the receiver's junction; each leg a Catmull-Rom curve through a midpoint displaced sideways). meander_amplitude: the midpoint's largest sideways displacement as a fraction of k (Phase E: of the link length, capped at 0.35 (k - 2) fine cells); the displacement is 0.5 to 1 times meander_amplitude x k x min(1, (Q / meander_reference_m3s)^meander_discharge_exponent), Q the upstream cell's discharge (exponent 0: no dependence). R3 (erosion run 9, windows A, B at k = 16 and C at k = 4): 0.2 (1.6 to 3.2 fine cells at k = 16, the legacy's 2 to 3 of 16); 0.3 drew more channel cells held above lower start surface (pillars > 130 m above the 8 neighbours' mean A 26, B 205, C 204 against 21, 166, 200), 0.15 fewer (A 18, B 159, C 203) with straighter legs; exponent 0.5 (reference 1000 m3/s) changed the counts by under 5 % (A 18, B 159, C 198), so 0 stays.
notes.regional.jitter_*: Erosion plan Phase R, R3: jitter_junction, the junction of a global cell's river lies within this fraction of k of the block's centre (a hash of the cell); jitter_edge_margin, a cardinal link's crossing point on the shared edge (a hash of the edge, so both cells agree) stays this fraction of k away from the cell's corners (legacy: 3 of 16; a diagonal link passes through the shared corner). R3 keeps the legacy values 0.25 and 0.1875. Multi-scale plan S3.10 (section 3, 'Channels without a lattice'): 0.5 (the junction anywhere in its block) and 0 (every fine cell of an edge equally likely at every k; a transit link's two edge points use the same rule), so no anchor of a link is tied to the global cells' lattice: an anchor jittered over less than a full cell period keeps the lattice's first harmonic (the S3.7 stage trace: diagonal links through the corners printed a NW-SE lattice peak of 48 at 109 km on window B at level 1). Measured on erosion run 9 (out/scratch/multiscale/s3.10, the largest lattice peak of the channel mask at levels 1 / 2): margin 0.0625 B16 4.63 / 2.82, C16 7.65 / 6.46 (at k 4 it floors to the edge cells with probabilities 0.21, 0.29, 0.29, 0.21; at k 16 never to the end cells); margin 0 B16 1.70 / 1.92, C16 3.49 / 2.08, A64 3.38 / 1.85; keeping a transit link's edge points off the half (quarter) of the edge next to the shared corner raised them (C16 13.5 / 5.3 and 13.8 / 5.3), so they stay uniform. The R3 geometry: --set landscape.regional.jitter_junction=0.25 --set landscape.regional.jitter_edge_margin=0.1875 --set landscape.regional.diagonal_transit=0.
notes.regional.diagonal_transit_tolerance_m: Multi-scale plan S3.10 (channel_network.hpp): when neither side cell of a diagonal link qualifies strictly (filled elevation between the link's two cells'), the eligible one (land, not c's receiver nor u's donor, draining to c's outlet) whose filled elevation misses that range by less is the transit block if the miss is at most this many metres; else the corner. Swept on erosion run 9 (out/scratch/multiscale/s3.10, table-4.txt; corner links of diagonal links, A16 / B16 / C16 / A64, and the largest level-1 lattice peak of the channel mask): 0 m 24 / 20 / 22 / 21 %, mask 3.49 / 2.35 / 6.95 / 5.22; 25 m 12 / 10 / 8 / 11 %, 1.88 / 2.23 / 4.91 / 3.08; 50 m 9 / 7 / 5 / 7 %, 2.05 / 2.23 / 3.71 / 2.92; 100 m 7 / 6 / 4 / 6 %, 2.05 / 2.23 / 3.58 / 2.92; border steps, forced parents and dried cells the same at every value. 100 m: the fewest corner links and the lowest peaks.
notes.regional.diagonal_transit: Multi-scale plan S3.10 (channel_network.hpp): 1 draws a diagonal global link u -> c through a transit block n, one of the two cells orthogonal to both (u + (dx, 0) or u + (0, dy)) that is land, whose filled elevation lies between c's and u's (no pinned trench through a higher block, no levee or dam across a lower one), that is neither c's receiver nor u's donor (no hairpin) and that drains to c's outlet on the global tree (both: a hash of the link): u's outflow leg to a hashed point on the edge u | n, a transit leg across n's block to a hashed point on the edge n | c, c's inflow leg from there, so no diagonal channel passes through the global cells' corners; where neither neighbour qualifies (a neck between basins, an X on a flat) the link steps through the shared corner as before, counted per level as cornerlinks beside diagonallinks (regional bundle). 0: every diagonal link through the shared corner (R3). Applies to the refinement loop and the single pass alike.
notes.regional.springs_per_cell: Erosion plan Phase R, R3: springs drawn from hashed points of a source cell's block (no pinned inflow), upstream of its junction, into its junction, carrying the cell's discharge and flows; 0 draws none. notes.refinement.factor: Multi-scale plan (docs/architecture/multiscale-plan.md, sections 1 and 3; S0.4 adds the group, nothing reads it before S2.3): level cells per parent cell edge of the refinement hierarchy; level L has factor^L cells per global cell edge. 4 by default for the smaller border step of the exact projection: a one-cell-wide channel line incised by I across a parent of factor^2 children gives lambda = I / factor and, the line at weight 0, lifts the land beside it by I / (factor - 1), I / 3 at factor 4 against I at factor 2 (a single incised cell: I / (factor^2 - 1)); 2 is allowed for the finer grading of levels; the S2.6 measurement decides.
notes.refinement.projection_weight_channel: Multi-scale plan, section 2 ('The exact projection, worked out'): the projection's weight on channel-bed cells, the others being 1 on free land and 0 on sea and lake beds. 0 keeps the channel beds where the level put them and lifts the land between them; a parent whose children all weigh 0 takes them all as 1.
notes.refinement.stored_scale_max: Multi-scale plan, section 1 ('Output at any resolution'): the finest scale k = factor^L written as a bundle; levels finer than that are render tiles computed on demand. 256 (about 600 m cells on a 256-column world) is level 4 at factor 4 and level 8 at factor 2: a scale, not a level count, so the rule holds at either factor.
notes.refinement.detail_cells: Multi-scale plan, section 3 ('Kernels'; refinement_levels.hpp, detaillevel): a detail of characteristic size s km runs at the coarsest level whose cell size is at most s / detail_cells, so a feature is resolved by at least detail_cells cells of its level (2: Nyquist). S2.6 or S3.0 may tune it.
notes.refinement.tile_cells: Multi-scale plan, Phase S4: a render tile's edge in level cells for the levels finer than stored_scale_max.
notes.refinement.smooth_*: Multi-scale plan, step S2.7 (section 3, 'S2.7: smooth before exact'; refinement_projection.hpp, smoothparentmeans): between the lakes and the exact projection every level smooths its per-parent correction with the projection's bounds, so the projection, which puts each parent's lambda back as a uniform shift of its children, only removes a small rest instead of printing the parent grid where the solve's lowering varies by kilometres between neighbours (regional runs 20 and 25). Per pass: mu_c = lambda_c x factor^2 / the rates of the children with room, Lambda = smooth_relaxation x the Catmull-Rom interpolation of mu at the child centres, each child moves rate x Lambda, its total capped at its headrooms (beds never move; sea, lake and dry land stay on their sides of their water). smooth_relaxation 1.4: the parent mean of an interpolated mode lies in [0.39, 1], so Richardson's optimum shrinks every mode by at most 0.44 per pass (the design's figure for the unbounded linear operator; caps at coasts and lakes break it). smooth_passes 6 leave about 0.7 percent of the largest lambda step (5.5 km on erosion run 9 to about 40 m); 0 turns the smoothing off (the S2.3 loop bit for bit). Each pass reaches 2 parent cells: a hierarchy run's halo is at least 2 x regional.mean_passes + 2 + 2 x smooth_passes global cells (26; the region command raises regional.halo_cells to it for a hierarchy run, the single pass keeps halo_cells).
notes.refinement.smooth_basis: Multi-scale plan, step S3.2's fallback (section 3, 'Phase S3 re-planned'; S3.0 adds the key, nothing reads it before S3.2): the interpolation basis of smoothparentmeans' total move, 0 the Catmull-Rom spline of S2.7 (C1: its curvature jumps on lines through the parent centres, the parent-period ripple of S2.7's review) and 1 a cubic B-spline (C2), taken if the ripple stays after S3.2's solve against its parent. 0 keeps S2.7's smoothing bit for bit. notes.regional.catchment_reach_global_cells: Multi-scale plan, step S3.9 (section 3, 'Seamless solve: a bounded catchment', with the review's local labelling; analytical_relief.hpp, regional_solve.hpp): r >= 1 bounds the solve's catchments in the refinement loop. Labels, once, on the start surface: one Priority-Flood per global cell g, seeded at the pinned cells in g's block and confined to the global cells within r of g; each unpinned cell takes the seed with the smallest (filled level, hops from the seed in that flood, hashed absolute key of the seed) over the floods reaching it; every pass routes inside the label, with hashed tie keys in every queue; a cell no flood reaches, or whose path in its winning flood leaves its label, keeps its start (unreachedcells); every land sink's junction is pinned (sinkjunctions). Bound: a label reads the cells within 2r global cells, a catchment lies within 2r of each of its cells and its extent reads their labels, so the solve reads cells within 4r: margin 4r - 2 = 2 global cells at r = 1 (refinement_grid.hpp, solvemargin), the same domain as r = 0. 0: the unbounded solve of S3.8 bit for bit; the single pass never bounds its catchments. notes.regional.tributary_*: Multi-scale plan, step S3.3 (regional_tributaries.hpp; S3.0 adds the keys off, nothing reads them before S3.3; the numbers from the S3.0 survey, plan section 6 'Learned in S3'): tributaries grown per level from the level's channels (Genevaux et al. 2013's growth from a network: there Horton-Strahler numbers are priority indices of a growth grammar, not ratios), hashed by the absolute key, lengths in [2 level cells, one parent cell), pinned with beds and discharge. tributary_enabled 0: none (the S2 pass exactly). tributary_spacing_km: the target valley spacing on the ground until S3.6's geosphere.valley_spacing field; Perron, Kirchner and Dietrich 2009 (Nature 460, 502-505) give a first-order spacing of 6.4 to 12.7 Lc with Lc = (D/K)^(1/(2m+1)), 30 to 320 m at five field sites (Dragon's Back 30, Point of the Mountain 54, Napa Valley 128, Gabilan Mesa 163, Eaton Hollow 321 m); 0.13 km is their median, finer than any stored level (k 64 cells are 2.4 km on a 256-column world), so the density rises towards it with the level and coarser levels need the Hack/Horton hierarchy. tributary_hack_exponent: h in Hack's law L = C A^h, 0.55 to 0.7 (Tarboton 1996), slightly below 0.6 in most basins: 0.57. tributary_hack_coefficient: C in km per km2^h; 1.27 is Hack's L = 1.4 A^0.6 in miles and square miles converted to km (S3.3: the conversion checked, 1.609 x 1.4 / 2.59^0.6 = 1.27; Hack's 1.4 and 0.6 themselves from memory, unverified; the coefficient belongs to h 0.6, not 0.57). At every level run the Hack length exceeds one parent cell, so the lengths are capped there and C and h set only the tributaries' Hack catchments (their discharge). tributary_junction_angle_deg: the mean angle between a tributary and the upstream direction of its receiving channel; 72 is the mean junction angle reported for humid climates (Seybold, Rothman and Kirchner 2017, from memory, unverified). tributary_angle_spread: each tributary's angle is the mean times 1 + spread x a hashed value in [-1, 1) (S3.3's choice, not tuned: enough to keep rows of tributaries off the grid's directions). tributary_node_margin: an inherited tributary's node in each of its parent cells is a hashed child at least floor(margin x factor) cells from the parent cell's edge (0.25: the inner 2 x 2 children at factor 4), so the redrawn line stays off the parent cells' borders. tributary_length_min_fraction: a tributary's target length is its capped Hack length times a hashed value in [min_fraction, 1) (0.75: lengths of 3 to 4 cells at factor 4; at least 2 cells always). The bifurcation ratio of S3.0 is not used (Genevaux et al. 2013 use none): removed in S3.3's review.
